summary: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Geshe degree at Menri Monastery and affiliated schools. He served as president of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, was a Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University, and founded Ligmincha International.
Teodor Iordănescu was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bucharest and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel, Richard Schmidt, and Eugen Hultzsch.

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later serving as Professor of Music at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.
Terence Dukes was a Buddhist studies specialist who founded Kongoryuji Temple in 1978 and taught there.

Terese Tse Bartholomew is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology who earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles. She served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum.
Terry Kleeman is a sinologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia. Around 2000, he became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder.
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held positions at Nihon University, Tohoku University—where he was dean of literature and president—Miyagi University of Education, Keio University, and Komazawa University.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Florida, Florida State University, and the University of Virginia. She taught at the University of Virginia and IUPUI, and became a professor of religion at FSU in 1993.
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Addey and Stanhope School and University College London.

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, where he later became professor emeritus. He also served as a professor at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University.
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and in Germany under Fischer, Wundt, and Zeller, later serving as professor at Tokyo, Toyo University, and president of Daito Bunka University.

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Waseda University and Komazawa University. He held multiple leadership roles, including president of Komazawa University, Komazawa Junior College, and Tohoku Fukushi University, as well as director of Soto Zen Research Center.
Tetsuro Noguchi was a sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies scholar who held academic posts at Yokohama National University, the University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

Tetsuro Watsuji was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He taught at Keio, Tsuda, Hosei, and Toyo, and held ethics chairs at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo.

Tetsuzo Tanikawa was a philosophy and Japanology scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at Doshisha University and served as a professor at Hosei University from approximately 1938 to 1965.
Teun Goudriaan is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Jan Gonda and served as a committee member and Professor Emeritus at Utrecht University.
Thanissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar who graduated from Oberlin College and studied under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko. He founded Metta Forest Monastery and became its abbot in 1993.
Thanon Chitkament is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Vishwas D. Gogte and P. S. Joshi.
